title: What survives when the window closes?
question: Can an isolated browser experiment retain its origin, present state and history without confusing elapsed time with work actually simulated?
method: Immutable reference-clock facade, add-only Birth records, versioned Present and History checkpoint transactions, and recorded full-process restart comparisons.
finding: The recorded graceful browser restart checks retained the Birth and complete History and restored the committed scene; a paused return performed no physics catch-up.
claim_scope: Isolated AREPO017 application rules and recorded completed-transaction/graceful-restart tests; not authenticated time or crash-proof permanent memory.
limitations: Device UTC is not independently authenticated; clock changes and OS sleep were not qualified.
Storage may be evicted. Durability extends only to the latest completed transaction; crashes and power loss were not tested.
Stale-revision refusal is not a simultaneous-tabs or forced-I/O-failure qualification.
Historical Safari seal remains UNKNOWN. No closed-browser physics, growth, learning, cryptographic identity or live-site integration is claimed.
open_questions: What additional evidence is needed for interrupted writes, storage eviction and device-time discontinuities?
